questions.question: What does Lady Macbeth fear will prevent Macbeth from taking the quickest path to the crown?

options.text: His kindness will restrain his ambition.
His fear of Banquo’s heirs will restrain him.
His wish to flee to England will restrain him.
His reliance on the apparitions will restrain him.

questions.explanation: She judges him ambitious but too full of human kindness to take the nearest way.

evidence.exact:
Glamis thou art, and Cawdor; and shalt be
What thou art promis’d. Yet do I fear thy nature;
It is too full o’ th’ milk of human kindness
To catch the nearest way. Thou wouldst be great;
Art not without ambition, but without
The illness should attend it. What thou wouldst highly,
That wouldst thou holily; wouldst not play false,
And yet wouldst wrongly win. Thou’dst have, great Glamis,
That which cries, “Thus thou must do,” if thou have it;
And that which rather thou dost fear to do,
Than wishest should be undone. Hie thee hither,
That I may pour my spirits in thine ear,
And chastise with the valour of my tongue
All that impedes thee from the golden round,
Which fate and metaphysical aid doth seem
To have thee crown’d withal.

questions.question: Why does Macbeth say he should protect Duncan during Duncan’s visit?

options.text: His trust in the witches requires him to wait for Banquo’s heirs.
His ties as kinsman, subject, and host require him to protect Duncan.
His duty to Malcolm requires him to leave Scotland immediately.
His rivalry with Macduff requires him to defend Dunsinane.

questions.explanation: Macbeth names family, allegiance, and hospitality as obligations against killing Duncan.

evidence.exact:
MACBETH.
If it were done when ’tis done, then ’twere well
It were done quickly. If th’ assassination
Could trammel up the consequence, and catch
With his surcease success; that but this blow
Might be the be-all and the end-all—here,
But here, upon this bank and shoal of time,
We’d jump the life to come. But in these cases
We still have judgement here; that we but teach
Bloody instructions, which being taught, return
To plague th’ inventor. This even-handed justice
Commends th’ ingredience of our poison’d chalice
To our own lips. He’s here in double trust:
First, as I am his kinsman and his subject,
Strong both against the deed; then, as his host,
Who should against his murderer shut the door,
Not bear the knife myself. Besides, this Duncan
Hath borne his faculties so meek, hath been
So clear in his great office, that his virtues
Will plead like angels, trumpet-tongued, against
The deep damnation of his taking-off;
And pity, like a naked new-born babe,
Striding the blast, or heaven’s cherubin, hors’d
Upon the sightless couriers of the air,
Shall blow the horrid deed in every eye,
That tears shall drown the wind.—I have no spur
To prick the sides of my intent, but only
Vaulting ambition, which o’erleaps itself
And falls on th’ other—

questions.question: How does Lady Macbeth propose to make Duncan vulnerable to murder?

options.text: Send Duncan’s sons to England and Ireland.
Hire murderers to ambush Banquo and Fleance.
Make his chamberlains drunk and blame them.
Send soldiers to seize Macduff’s castle.

questions.explanation: Her plan disables the chamberlains with drink and places the guilt on them.

evidence.exact:
LADY MACBETH.
We fail?
But screw your courage to the sticking-place,
And we’ll not fail. When Duncan is asleep
(Whereto the rather shall his day’s hard journey
Soundly invite him), his two chamberlains
Will I with wine and wassail so convince
That memory, the warder of the brain,
Shall be a fume, and the receipt of reason
A limbeck only: when in swinish sleep
Their drenched natures lie as in a death,
What cannot you and I perform upon
Th’ unguarded Duncan? what not put upon
His spongy officers; who shall bear the guilt
Of our great quell?

questions.question: Why do Malcolm and Donalbain leave after Duncan’s death?

options.text: They believe Banquo’s heirs will inherit at once.
They trust Macbeth to make their position safe.
They hope to join Macduff’s attack on Fife.
They fear that the murderer will target them too.

questions.explanation: The brothers see hidden danger around them and separate for safety.

evidence.exact:
DONALBAIN.
To Ireland, I. Our separated fortune
Shall keep us both the safer. Where we are,
There’s daggers in men’s smiles: the near in blood,
The nearer bloody.
evidence.prefix: an does easy. I’ll to England.

evidence.exact:
MALCOLM.
This murderous shaft that’s shot
Hath not yet lighted; and our safest way
Is to avoid the aim. Therefore to horse;
And let us not be dainty of leave-taking,
But shift away. There’s warrant in that theft
Which steals itself, when there’s no mercy left.

questions.question: Why does Macbeth see Banquo’s descendants as a threat to his kingship?

options.text: The witches predicted a line of kings from Banquo.
Duncan named Banquo Prince of Cumberland.
Macduff proclaimed Fleance king at the banquet.
Malcolm offered Banquo command of Dunsinane.

questions.explanation: Macbeth fears that his own crown will pass to the line the witches promised Banquo.

evidence.exact:
To be thus is nothing,
But to be safely thus. Our fears in Banquo
Stick deep, and in his royalty of nature
Reigns that which would be fear’d: ’tis much he dares;
And, to that dauntless temper of his mind,
He hath a wisdom that doth guide his valour
To act in safety. There is none but he
Whose being I do fear: and under him
My genius is rebuk’d; as, it is said,
Mark Antony’s was by Caesar. He chid the sisters
When first they put the name of king upon me,
And bade them speak to him; then, prophet-like,
They hail’d him father to a line of kings:
Upon my head they plac’d a fruitless crown,
And put a barren sceptre in my gripe,
Thence to be wrench’d with an unlineal hand,
No son of mine succeeding. If’t be so,
For Banquo’s issue have I fil’d my mind;
For them the gracious Duncan have I murder’d;
Put rancours in the vessel of my peace
Only for them; and mine eternal jewel
Given to the common enemy of man,
To make them kings, the seed of Banquo kings!
Rather than so, come, fate, into the list,
And champion me to th’ utterance!—Who’s there?—

questions.question: What sight disrupts Macbeth’s behavior at the banquet?

options.text: The bloody child that promises him safety.
Banquo’s ghost sitting in his place.
The armed head that warns against Macduff.
The line of kings shown by the witches.

questions.explanation: The ghost occupies Macbeth’s seat, and Macbeth addresses its bloody appearance.

questions.question: What does Macbeth resolve to do on learning that Macduff has fled to England?

options.text: Send murderers to ambush Banquo and Fleance.
Visit the witches to demand their first prophecy.
Attack Macduff’s castle and kill his family.
Abandon Dunsinane and escape to Ireland.

questions.explanation: He resolves to seize Fife and put Macduff’s wife and children to the sword.

evidence.exact:
MACBETH.
Time, thou anticipat’st my dread exploits:
The flighty purpose never is o’ertook
Unless the deed go with it. From this moment
The very firstlings of my heart shall be
The firstlings of my hand. And even now,
To crown my thoughts with acts, be it thought and done:
The castle of Macduff I will surprise;
Seize upon Fife; give to th’ edge o’ th’ sword
His wife, his babes, and all unfortunate souls
That trace him in his line. No boasting like a fool;
This deed I’ll do before this purpose cool:
But no more sights!—Where are these gentlemen?
Come, bring me where they are.

questions.question: What preoccupies Lady Macbeth during her sleepwalking?

options.text: Banquo’s ghost taking a seat at the banquet.
A moving forest approaching Dunsinane hill.
A dagger leading her toward Duncan’s room.
Blood on her hands that she cannot clean away.

questions.explanation: Her speech returns to blood and the impossible cleaning of her hands.

questions.question: Why does Malcolm order his soldiers to carry branches from Birnam Wood?

options.text: To hide the army’s numbers from observers.
To provide timber for repairing Dunsinane’s defenses.
To mark a safe route for the army’s retreat.
To display a sign of submission to Macbeth.

questions.explanation: The branches will hide the army’s numbers from observers.

evidence.exact:
MALCOLM.
Let every soldier hew him down a bough,
And bear’t before him. Thereby shall we shadow
The numbers of our host, and make discovery
Err in report of us.

questions.question: What does Macduff reveal that overturns Macbeth’s confidence in his charmed life?

options.text: His wife and children have been murdered.
He was cut prematurely from his mother’s womb.
Malcolm’s army is approaching Dunsinane.
Fleance has escaped the hired murderers.

questions.explanation: Macduff’s unusual birth exposes the misleading assurance on which Macbeth relies.

evidence.exact:
MACBETH.
Thou losest labour:
As easy mayst thou the intrenchant air
With thy keen sword impress, as make me bleed:
Let fall thy blade on vulnerable crests;
I bear a charmed life, which must not yield
To one of woman born.

MACDUFF.
Despair thy charm;
And let the angel whom thou still hast serv’d
Tell thee, Macduff was from his mother’s womb
Untimely ripp’d.
